records.name: The Friendly Sons and Daughters of St. Patrick
records.summary: An Irish heritage society founded in Philadelphia in 1771. Members gather for quarterly dinner meetings with Irish music and a guest speaker, and the society supports charitable causes.
records.what_you_do: Attend the quarterly dinner meetings, welcome new members at induction, and take part in the society's charitable work.

schedule.text: Quarterly meetings with dinner, 6 to 9 pm. The most recent dated meeting was the Winter 2026 meeting on February 4, 2026.

cost.text: $55 per person for the Winter 2026 meeting. Tickets for that meeting are closed.

first_step.how: Use the Join the Society link on the group's website. The page does not say who is eligible, so ask the society before planning on it.
first_step.basis: Membership is by induction, and the page does not describe eligibility or how to apply.

records.notes: Founded in Philadelphia but meets in Havertown in Delaware County, so in_city is false. The page lists no society email or phone, only a link to a contact page that was not read. Winter season reflects the only dated meeting on the page.

records.name: Philly Japanese Conversation Club
records.summary: A free conversation club for Japanese and English speakers of every level, run by the Japan America Society of Greater Philadelphia. Members practice by joining live online discussions led by society staff.
records.what_you_do: Join the online discussions, practice Japanese or English with other members, and talk through the topics staff bring.

schedule.text: Live online discussions twice a month. The page gives no weekday or time, and its only dated session is from July 2020.

locations.label: Japan America Society office (for mail and questions)

first_step.how: Join the Philly Japanese Conversation Club Facebook group, as the page directs
first_step.basis: Free and open to speakers of all levels, with a stated way to join

records.notes: The newest dated item on the page is a July 7, 2020 session, and the page calls the club virtual. Current activity could not be confirmed, so status is dormant. Check with the society before relying on it.

records.name: Northeast Philadelphia Chinese Association
records.summary: A grassroots nonprofit that supports Asian American residents of Northeast Philadelphia with cultural, learning and economic growth. Its newest dated item on the website is a July 2022 anniversary note.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer with the group or attend its community events. The website links to volunteering and donation pages.

first_step.how: Call 267-225-4628 or email nepca.chinese@gmail.com to ask about events and volunteering
first_step.basis: The website does not say how to join, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The site is reachable but the only dated item is from July 2022. The event calendar, blog and news pages are linked but their contents were not readable. Older press from 2018 and 2019 gave a Castor Avenue address that may be out of date, so no street address is recorded. The group is under the fiscal sponsorship of the Culture Trust of Greater Philadelphia.

records.name: Deaf-Hearing Communication Centre
records.summary: A center that teaches American Sign Language classes and works for equal communication access across the Philadelphia region. It also holds Deaf community social events, such as a bingo and ASL night.
records.what_you_do: Take an ASL class, practice signing at community social events, or ask about interpreting and access services.

schedule.text: Events are posted with dates but no years. Examples on the site: a Deaf Day at the Philadelphia Zoo on September 20, and a Bingo and ASL Social on November 21. Class times are not on the home page.

cost.text: Not listed on the home page

first_step.how: Email Info@dhcc.org or call 610-604-0452 to ask about the next ASL class or event

records.notes: The site footer reads 2024 and the event entries show no year, so current status is unknown. Class length, cost and locations were not on the home page and are not recorded. Earlier press describes classes at several sites across Delaware, Montgomery and Philadelphia counties, so an in-city class is not confirmed. The ASL classes page was linked but not fetched.

leads_only.note: Library calendar listings for free English conversation tables, some with no registration. Calendar pages returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so the schedules come only from search snippets and were not recorded. These are library programs, so a fetch from another route is needed.

leads_only.name: Deaf and Signing Community Gathering (Joseph E. Coleman Northwest Regional Library)
leads_only.note: Listed as a monthly Saturday gathering with an interpreter. The calendar page returned HTTP 403, so it was not verified.

leads_only.name: Free Library of Philadelphia adult ESL and literacy classes (Community College of Philadelphia partnership, Wyoming and Paschalville branches)
leads_only.note: Snippets mention registration and placement tests. Not fetched, and class schedules change by term.

leads_only.name: PhillyASLMeetup (ASL conversation group)
leads_only.note: Meetup-based group. Only 2021 event listings were found. Meetup is a lead source only, so the group's own page was not confirmed.

leads_only.name: Breakthrough: Deaf Advocacy ASL club at uCity Square
leads_only.note: A twice-monthly ASL practice club listing with no date. Lead only, not verified.

leads_only.name: DeafCAN! Deaf Community Action Network
leads_only.note: Serves Deaf and hard of hearing refugees, immigrants and asylees in southeastern Pennsylvania, with free ASL, English and citizenship classes. The group's own website was not found in search. Next step: find its site.

leads_only.name: Korean American Association of Greater Philadelphia
leads_only.note: Marked its 50th anniversary event in Blue Bell, Montgomery County. Its own website was not found.

leads_only.name: Society of Young Korean Americans (Jenkintown)
leads_only.note: Formed in 2011, based in Jenkintown, accepts individual and community members. Idealist is a lead source only, and the group is in Montgomery County, not the city.

leads_only.name: Korean Community Development Service Center
leads_only.note: Listed at 6055 North 5th Street, Philadelphia 19120. Found only on a federal listing. Its own website and current programs were not checked.

leads_only.name: Filipino American Association of Philadelphia (FAAPI)
leads_only.note: Founded in 1912 for heritage preservation, with a Filipino Community Center. Source is a 2012 press release on Scribd. The group's own website must be found and checked.

leads_only.name: Filipino Executive Council of Greater Philadelphia
leads_only.note: Umbrella group for Filipino community events. Mentioned in a news item only. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Polish Heritage Society of Philadelphia
leads_only.note: Hosted the 78th annual convention of the American Council for Polish Culture in Philadelphia in August 2026. Its own website was not found. Check for a membership or events page.

leads_only.name: American Council for Polish Culture
leads_only.note: Fetched. The page does not state the headquarters city, and the group looks national. Not recorded because its Philadelphia tie is unclear.

leads_only.name: Federation of Hellenic-American Societies of Philadelphia and Greater Delaware
leads_only.note: Organizes the Greek Independence Parade (April 2026) and a Greek community fund. Its own website was not checked.

leads_only.name: African Cultural Alliance of North America (ACANA)
leads_only.note: A 501(c)(3) at 5530 Chester Avenue offering social and legal services, community programs and African and Caribbean arts events. The PA 211 listing was found but the agency's own site was not identified.

leads_only.name: African Family Health Organization (AFAHO)
leads_only.note: Welcoming space for African and Caribbean immigrants and refugees. Youth and adult education programs. The group's own website was not found.

leads_only.name: Nationalities Service Center
leads_only.note: Immigrant services with short- and long-term volunteer openings. Its own site was not found in search. Likely a service agency, not a club, so decide the family fit when checked.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Office of Immigrant Affairs (Week of Welcoming, Welcome Center volunteers)
leads_only.note: City office. The Week of Welcoming brings long-time and newer residents together. Check the city's own pages for current volunteer openings.

leads_only.name: Southeast Asian Mutual Assistance Association Coalition (SEAMAAC)
leads_only.note: Mentioned as partner for adult basic education with ACANA. Its own website was not checked.

leads_only.name: Puentes de Salud
leads_only.note: Health and wellness for Latinx immigrants, with volunteer roles. Health-focused, so it may fit another family better. Not checked.

leads_only.name: GALAEI
leads_only.note: Spanish translation, interpretation and mental health support for immigrant families. Service agency. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Strictly Speaking (cultural exchange and face-to-face pen pals, Philadelphia area)
leads_only.note: Idealist listing only. Idealist is a lead source. The group's own site was not found.

leads_only.name: MyLanguageExchange.com (Philadelphia partner listings)
leads_only.note: A partner-matching website, not a group. Listed here only as a lead source for one-on-one practice partners. Not recorded.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation (Vietnamese Women's Health Project, Vietnamese Elder Wellness Project)
leads_only.note: Social services nonprofit with Vietnamese community programs. Not a membership club. Its program pages were not checked.

notes: Ran out of WebSearch budget at 10 of 10, so the family coverage is thin. Four records are checked. Most leads on Free Library, Korean, Filipino, Polish, Greek and Vietnamese groups need a second pass with more search budget or direct site fetches. Two of the four publish records (Japan America Society club, Northeast Philadelphia Chinese Association) are dormant, and one (Deaf-Hearing Communication Centre) has an unknown status. The Free Library English and ESL programs are the largest gap: the calendar was blocked, so they are only leads. Searches found no Philadelphia Saturday heritage language school other than Korean ones studied in academic papers from 2013 and earlier, so none were recorded.
